title: AetherWorks cost sprint — POC scoping and benchmark planning
next_steps: Alex to send detailed cost-model spreadsheet and assumptions (2026-04-01)
Maya to run a 1-hour latency/throughput baseline on Redwood hosted (slot) and share traces (2026-03-30)
Customer to provide representative traffic traces and 200 sample prompts (2026-03-29)
Schedule security deep-dive with product security (if POC greenlit) (week of 2026-04-06)
action_items: Alex Romero: Share cost model spreadsheet + example calculations (due 2026-04-01)
Maya Chen: Run small hosted benchmark (3 model variants) and upload perf logs (due 2026-03-30)
Sam O'Neil: Export 7 days of request traces and token histograms from prod proxy (due 2026-03-29)
Priya Singh: Confirm procurement lead and budget constraints (due 2026-03-31)
summary: Discovery/Poc scoping focused on unit economics for a conversational assistant — agree to run a short cost/latency benchmark using 3 model variants, capture batching and caching behavior, and produce a per-token and per-session cost model. Key constraints: p95 latency < 200ms for short prompts, monthly budget cap $12k for hosted POC, data residency in us-west, SOC2 requirement. Next step: Redwood to deliver cost spreadsheet and run hosted baseline; customer to deliver traffic traces and sample prompts.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey Jordan, Priya, Sam — thanks for carving out time. quick agenda — alignment on success criteria, then sizing and bench plans, and last section costs and next steps.
[00:00:18] Jordan (AetherWorks CTO): Yeah thanks, Alex. We're tight on budget for the spike but need to validate that cost per active user is acceptable. goal is a conversational assistant for our dashboard, light RAG, lots of short queries.
[00:00:34] Maya (Redwood SE): Quick clarifying q — when you say "short queries" what's median token size? prompts vs responses?
[00:00:42] Sam (AetherWorks ML): median prompt ~35 tokens, responses are typically 50-120 tokens depending on context. but we have very spiky traffic — a few power users at 10 rps per user during peak.
[00:00:55] Priya (Eng Mgr): Our constraint is monthly POC budget ~12k, and we need to show a path to <$0.0005 per token or equivalent if possible.
[00:01:07] Alex: Good, that budget context is helpful. rough back-of-envelope: at $0.0006/token that's about 20M tokens for 12k — but ofc batching and cache can reduce effective cost.
[00:01:22] Jordan: Can you explain the knobs you'd flip to hit something like $0.0004? quantization? batching?
[00:01:29] Maya: Sure — main levers are model selection, quantization (int8/int4), batching (amortize kernels across requests), & KV/prefix caching for repeated context. For short prompts, batching has diminishing returns beyond ~64 conc but can help at moderate QPS. caching helps a lot for deterministic prefixes — e.g., system prompts or template expansions.
[00:01:50] Sam: We do have a lot of repeated boilerplate, so prefix caching could be a big win. how do you estimate cache hit rate impact?
[00:01:58] Diego (Redwood Solutions): We model hit rate as simple factor — effective tokens served = tokens * (1 - hit_rate). So at 40% hit rate you cut token bill 40%. but latency interaction matters — cold misses cost more.
[00:02:12] Jordan: Ok, what about latencies — our SLO target for short-turn conv is p95 < 200ms, ideally 150ms. is that realistic with batching and caching?
[00:02:21] Maya: With hosted GPU inference and small models we can often hit ~120–180ms p95 with aggressive KV cache and batching < 16ms queueing. But for larger models or heavy RAG it's higher. We should benchmark three variants: compact quantized model, mid-size unquantized, and a streaming-large fallback.
[00:02:41] Priya: That sounds fine. how long for the benchmark and what do you need from us?
[00:02:47] Alex: Ideally 1 hour hosted run for each variant with representative traffic and concurrency pattern. you provide sample prompts & token histogram; we'll provide a harness and run from us-west to match your region.
[00:02:58] Sam: We'll export two days of traces. question: you mentioned per-session amortization. how do we account for KV cache memory vs cost?
[00:03:08] Maya: We factor host costs + GPU time; KV cache reduces token compute but increases memory use on the instance. For Dedicated we'd size GPU memory accordingly; in hosted the runtime manages cache allocation and we model it in the spreadsheet as an incremental cost if it forces a larger instance class.
[00:03:26] Jordan: Could you walk through a sample per-1M token calculation?
[00:03:30] Alex: Sure — sample quick calc: baseline model cost to run = $X/hour. assume throughput 1.5M tokens/hour on a given instance and instance cost $4/hr amortized across customers = $4 / 1.5M = $0.0000027 / token plus model license / infra margin and storage etc — we round to $0.0004–$0.0008 token depending on model and quant. then add OpenAI/Anthropic-like pricing parity if using external vendors. that's simplified but spreadsheet will show line-items.
[00:04:05] Priya: That placeholder math seems optimistic — can you include network egress, KV storage, and dev ops time?
[00:04:12] Diego: Yes we'll include network egress assumptions (we use conservative 30KB avg per response), and a small ops uplift (~15%) in the model.
[00:04:20] Sam: About batching — what batch size would you recommend for our 10 rps power users with spikes to 200 rps?
[00:04:26] Maya: For spiky loads, dynamic batching with a short batching window (4–8ms) works — aim for batch sizes 8–32 during peaks. but you need a QoS policy to prioritize latency-sensitive small requests (user interactive). Redwood's router can route by policy to keep tail latency bounded.
[00:04:41] Jordan: Cool. what about fallback — if dedicated capacity maxes out do you spill to lower-cost model?
[00:04:47] Alex: Yes — we recommend model-tier fallback: try compact quantized first, then a mid model, and if both unavailable queue or degrade gracefully. we'll include an autoscaling + fallback policy in POC config.
[00:04:58] Priya: Security questions: we need SOC2, SSO, and audit logs. can Redwood supply SOC2 and KMS options for hosted POC?
[00:05:07] Diego: Redwood has SOC2 Type II, SAML/SSO is supported, and KMS integration for customer-owned keys is available in Private/Dedicated. for hosted POC we can offer envelope encryption and audit logs; we'll flag any restricted data flows in the plan.
[00:05:22] Sam: Good. For the benchmark harness — can you simulate user sessions with conversation history that uses KV cache friendly patterns?
[00:05:29] Maya: Yes, include conversation templates and system prompts in the sample set; we can toggle cache hit rates in the harness. we'll run three sweeps: no cache, 30% hit, 60% hit.
[00:05:39] Jordan: What about quantization— any model family you recommend?
[00:05:43] Maya: For short-turn dialogue we often start with a 7B family quantized to int8 or int4; if you need higher quality go to 13B but costs jump ~2–3x. We'll include quality vs cost deltas in the report with automated evals on your sample prompts.
[00:05:58] Priya: Can you include evaluation metrics — like answer correctness and hallucination rates?
[00:06:02] Alex: Yes — expected outputs: per-variant latency distribution, tokens consumed, per-token cost, per-session cost, and simple QA metrics (exact-match or BLEU-style) plus hallucination notes from small eval set.
[00:06:14] Sam: One pain point is cold-starts — some of our users do infrequent heavy queries. does caching help there?
[00:06:19] Maya: Not for cold-start of unseen context. for infrequent heavy queries, we propose a caching TTL strategy and pre-warming for top queries. also allow burst capacity in Dedicated mode.
[00:06:31] Jordan: Alright rough timeline?
[00:06:34] Alex: If you deliver traces by Monday (2026-03-29), we can run hosted baseline Wednesday–Thursday (2026-03-30/31) and deliver a cost + perf report by 2026-04-01. Procurement/security deep-dive the week of 2026-04-06.
[00:06:47] Priya: That timeline works. procurement will need a formal SOW to sign — is that standard?
[00:06:52] Diego: We'll provide a POC SOW covering duration, budget cap, and confidentiality; template will be attached to the follow-up email.
[00:06:59] Sam: A few nitty bits — how do you capture per-token accounting for streaming responses? partial tokens?
[00:07:06] Maya: We account per-submitted token + model-generated tokens. streaming doesn't change token accounting, just the delivery. The runtime counts token boundaries and we reconcile with your proxy logs.
[00:07:16] Jordan: I sometimes see model side costs (KV memory) not exposed in external APIs — how transparent will that be?
[00:07:21] Diego: For POC we'll show the stamped instance types and memory footprints per-run; transparency is part of the report.
[00:07:28] Alex: Ok let's capture success criteria out loud — Jordan?
[00:07:31] Jordan: p95 latency <= 200ms for median prompts, cost per monthly active user < $2 at 100 MAU normalized to our usage, and clear path to production with SOC2 and KMS.
[00:07:43] Priya: Add an operational acceptance — runbook for how to triage high latency incidents.
[00:07:47] Maya: We'll include a short runbook and recommended SLO alerts.
[00:07:51] Sam: Anything else on billing — do you support usage caps and alerts?
[00:07:55] Alex: Yes hosted accounts can have hard caps and predictive alerts; we'll demonstrate during POC.
[00:07:59] Jordan: Ok let's talk numbers real quick — can you put a sample bucketed estimate for 1M tokens with different cache hits and batchings?
[00:08:06] Diego: Quick verbal example: compact quantized model: base compute ~$0.00035/token, with 40% cache hit effective token cost drops to ~$0.00021. mid model unquantized: ~$0.0007/token -> with 40% hit -> ~$0.00042. These are example deltas; spreadsheet will be explicit.
[00:08:25] Priya: That would translate to what monthly spend at 10M tokens?
[00:08:28] Maya: 10M tokens at $0.00035 -> $3.5k baseline; with hits maybe $2.1k. mid model would be $7k -> $4.2k. add networking & margins and you're in $2.5–$8k ranges.
[00:08:43] Sam: Sound reasonable. one more: do you model cost of embedding calls for RAG separately?
[00:08:48] Alex: Yes embeddings are modeled separately — per-embedding calls have different token and vector cost and should be budgeted; for the POC we'll either mock or run a small embed pipeline and include costs.
[00:08:58] Jordan: Cool. I want the bench to include a failure/recovery test — what happens when instance OOMs or cache thrashes?
[00:09:05] Maya: We'll run a controlled failure test and capture degradation modes and time-to-recover; Redwood router has fallbacks.
[00:09:12] Priya: And SLA for POC?
[00:09:14] Diego: POC doesn't carry a full enterprise SLA but we'll commit to uptime during benchmark windows and provide logs. For production Dedicated we can discuss SLA.
[00:09:22] Alex: Ok, wrap-up: Alex to send the cost model + SOW template, Maya will run hosted benches when traces arrive, customer to provide traces and sample prompts. Any final Qs?
[00:09:33] Jordan: none, thanks team.
[00:09:35] Alex: Great, we'll follow up by email with attachments and calendar invites. thanks everyone.

Note: transcription contains occasional mis-hears (e.g., "K V cash" for KV cache), filler words, and speaker attribution may be slightly off in a few lines.
